newsitem.title: UK: Labour lead slips in latest British opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: Labour lead slips in latest British opinion poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has suffered a fall in its lead over the ruling Conservatives in the past month, said an opinion poll published on Friday.
The Gallup poll for the Daily Telegraph newspaper gave Labour 49 percent of the vote, down from 50.5 percent last month, while support for the Conservatives was up 1.5 points to 34 percent.
The minority Liberal Democrats had 10.5 percent of the vote, up 1.5 points.
The results would give Labour a 150-seat majority in the House of Commons (lower house of parliament) in a general election, the Telegraph said.
Prime Minister John Major, whose party has consistently lagged behind Labour by around 20 points in opinion polls for the last two years, must hold a general election by May 22.
The Telegraph said it believed the Conservatives' better opinion poll performance had been helped by a gradually improving "feelgood factor" over the economy.
